summary: The note describes the English seizure of New Netherland in 1664, when Richard Nicolls's four frigates arrived at New Amsterdam and met no resistance because Dutch defenses were inadequate and the West India Company had ignored pleas for reinforcement. Director Stuyvesant negotiated terms, and the Articles of Transfer guaranteed religious tolerance (Article VIII), though the English violated the Articles along the Delaware River under Sir Robert Carr. The note closes with the 1667 Treaty of Breda, which ended the Second Anglo-Dutch War and left New Netherland with the English.
one_line: Account of the 1664 English takeover of New Netherland, its negotiated Articles of Transfer, and the 1667 Treaty of Breda.
key_facts: On August 27, 1664, four English frigates led by Richard Nicolls sailed into New Amsterdam's harbor and demanded New Netherland's surrender.
The English met no resistance when they arrived at New Amsterdam in August 1664.
Citizens of New Amsterdam had repeatedly requested protection by a suitable Dutch garrison against massacres by the natives.
The West India Company was indifferent to previous pleas for reinforcement of men and ships against English encroachments.
Stuyvesant negotiated successfully for good terms from his 'too powerful enemies'.
Article VIII of the Articles of Transfer secured religious tolerance, assuring New Netherlanders they 'shall keep and enjoy the liberty of their consciences in religion'.
The Articles of Transfer were largely observed in New Amsterdam and the Hudson River Valley.
The English immediately violated the Articles along the Delaware River, where pillaging, looting, and arson were undertaken under the orders of Sir Robert Carr, Kt.
Many Dutch settlers were sold into slavery in Virginia on Carr's orders.
An entire Mennonite settlement led by Pieter Corneliszoon Plockhoy near modern Lewes, Delaware was wiped out.
The 1667 Treaty of Breda ended the Second Anglo-Dutch War.
After the Treaty of Breda, the Dutch did not press their claims on New Netherland and the status quo was maintained.
Under the Treaty of Breda the Dutch kept Suriname and the nutmeg island of Run.
